eyebrow: Lesson 09 · B1 · Good Manners in Public · 20 câu
heading: Sharing Public Space
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Good Manners in Public – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 4–7.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Good Manners in Public (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: The moment you step out of your front door, you enter {public space|public space}. A public space is any place you share with other people: parks, shops, libraries, cinemas and restaurants are all examples. In fact, most of the places we visit every day are public.

paras.label: B
paras.text: Unfortunately, not everyone {behaves|behaves} politely in public. Have you ever been to the cinema and sat near people who talked loudly, used {bad language|bad language} or chatted on their phones during the film? How did it make you feel? Those people were not respecting your space.

paras.label: C
paras.text: You can do better. Keep your music and your voice down, and choose your words carefully. Throwing bad words around is like throwing rubbish around: after a while, everything starts to {stink|stink}.

paras.label: D
paras.text: Walking in busy places has its own rules. On a {crowded|crowded} {pavement|pavement} or in a school corridor, keep to one side and pass people carefully. Don't {be a hog|be a hog} by taking up all the space, and think about the people {stuck|stuck} behind you. If someone wants to get past, step to the side.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Last but not least, never {spit|spit} on the street: nobody wants to be splashed! In Australia, spitting is considered so rude that it is actually {against the law|against the law} in public places.

parts.title: Part 1 · Matching headings
parts.instr: Chọn tiêu đề phù hợp nhất cho mỗi đoạn. Có 2 tiêu đề thừa.
options: What counts as a public space
Watch your volume and your words
A habit that is even illegal somewhere
The best seats at the cinema

items.label: Paragraph A
items.why: Đoạn A định nghĩa không gian công cộng.

items.label: Paragraph B
items.why: Đoạn B: người nói to, chửi bậy ở rạp phim.

items.label: Paragraph C
items.why: Đoạn C: vặn nhỏ nhạc, giọng nói, chọn lời.

items.label: Paragraph D
items.why: Đoạn D: đi trên vỉa hè, hành lang đông người.

items.label: Paragraph E
items.why: Đoạn E: khạc nhổ bị cấm ở Úc.

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT given as an example of a public space?
questions.why: Phòng ngủ là không gian riêng, không được nêu.

questions.q: The writer says that everyone behaves well in public.
questions.why: Sai. *not everyone behaves politely in public.*

questions.q: In paragraph C, why are bad words compared to rubbish?
options: Both make a place unpleasant after a while.
Both are easy to pick up.
questions.why: *after a while, everything starts to stink.*

questions.q: What should you do if someone behind you wants to get past?
questions.why: *If someone wants to get past, step to the side.*

questions.q: In Australia, spitting in public can break the law.
questions.why: Đúng. *it is actually against the law in public places.*

questions.q: Why does the writer ask questions in paragraph B?
options: to make readers think about how rude behaviour feels
to find out where readers live
questions.why: Câu hỏi giúp người đọc tự cảm nhận việc bị làm phiền.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: Which paragraph describes the kind of behaviour in this picture?
questions.why: Đoạn B kể về người nói chuyện ồn ào trong rạp.
questions.alt: Children in cinema seats; a girl with glasses waves and chats while a boy with popcorn looks unhappy

questions.q: How does the boy with the popcorn probably feel?
questions.why: Cậu bé nhăn mặt vì bị làm phiền khi xem phim.
questions.alt: Children in cinema seats; a girl with glasses waves and chats while a boy with popcorn looks unhappy

questions.q: What is the most useful advice from paragraph D for these children?
options: Leave space for others and step aside to let people pass.
Walk in the middle and take up all the space.
Spit on the ground when nobody is looking.
questions.why: Đoạn D: *Don't be a hog… step to the side.*
questions.alt: Several children walking in different directions on a busy path

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: My grandfather walks slowly because he has a bad knee. [1] Last weekend, we were walking along a busy street when a group of teenagers came up behind us. [2] One of them even smiled and said, "Have a nice day!" [3]
options: Sometimes the people behind him get impatient.
Instead of pushing past, they waited until we moved to the side.
It reminded me that a little patience makes public spaces nicer for everyone.
They shouted bad words and spat on the ground.
My grandfather ran faster than all of them.

items.why: Đi chậm → người phía sau hay sốt ruột (chuẩn bị cho tình huống sau).
Nhóm thanh niên lịch sự chờ, phù hợp với lời chúc *Have a nice day* tiếp theo.
Kết: bài học về kiên nhẫn nơi công cộng.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *Don't be a hog by taking up all the space* (D). If you are **a hog**, you…
options: selfishly take more than your share
questions.why: **Hog** (con lợn) → người tham, chiếm hết chỗ.
Nghĩa bóng: mọi thứ trở nên khó chịu.

questions.q: *…it is actually against the law* (E). Something **against the law** is…
